card.name: Small words before an expected noun
card.fires_on: Small linking words (a, the, on, with, has, have) and partway-through word pieces, mostly in label text where the next word is highly predictable, such as 'has been reported' after an adverse reaction name.

modes.label: Has/have after reaction names
modes.description: The verb 'has' or 'have' right after a named adverse reaction, before 'been reported' or 'occurred'.
modes.example: Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS)<< has>> been reported in patients taking NSAIDs such

modes.label: Articles and prepositions mid-phrase
modes.description: 'a', 'the', 'on' or 'with' inside a descriptive clause, just before a predictable noun.
modes.example: simply connect it to a computer with<< a>> USB cable or power it with a

modes.label: Inside medical terms
modes.description: Partway through a medical term such as atrial or inhibitor.
modes.example: Cardiac Myosin Inhib<<itor>> Mavacamten Refer to the mav

card.writes: No clear output effect; the promoted and suppressed tokens look unrelated and mixed.
card.plain: It fires on small connecting words where the next word is easy to guess, such as 'has' before 'been reported'.
